replies.body:
Local Claude says this suggestion is not applicable:

There's no per-kaid failure to scope here — 
  ▎ ManyCoachedByActorErr makes a single manyCoachedBy 
  ▎ call for the whole set and returns an empty map on 
  ▎ any failure, so the error is genuinely total rather
  ▎ than one student's. Fanning it to every key is the
  ▎ accurate representation; scoping it per-kaid would
  ▎ mean inventing attribution that doesn't exist.
  ▎
  ▎ It also doesn't change the authorization outcome. 
  ▎ On error we log and fall through to the admin check
  ▎ — the same place we land on a legitimate "not 
  ▎ coached." And it matches the unbatched path: 
  ▎ acl.IsCoachedByActor already "returns false, and 
  ▎ additionally logs an error" on failure, so a 
  ▎ coaches-service outage denied the whole roster 
  ▎ before this change too.
  ▎
  ▎ The session loader scopes per-config because it 
  ▎ issues one query per config, so its failures really
  ▎ are partial. Different query structure, different 
  ▎ granularity — both loaders attribute errors to 
  ▎ exactly the keys they affect.

corrected.subject: The coaching batch can deny the whole roster after one student's lookup fails, so fall back per kaid on error.
corrected.discussion: The coaching loader fans a single failed lookup out to every kaid, so one student's transient error can deny the whole roster for a teacher without admin permission. ManyCoachedBy runs one lookup per student, then ManyCoachedByActorErr returns an empty map on an error and the loader marks every key failed. Keep the successful batch path. On batch failure, fall back per kaid using acl.IsCoachedByActorErr and retain each result and error in its own slot. The cached function variable exists in pkg/khan/acl/coaches.go:36-40. This adds calls only on the failure path and cannot repair a service-wide outage.
